result:
The proposed answer of 5 matches the results I recall from the literature, but I did not re-derive them and am relying on memory here.

- Pinchuk (1994) gave a non-injective polynomial local diffeomorphism of the plane, so a nowhere-vanishing Jacobian alone does not force injectivity.
- Injectivity is known when the degree of one component is at most 4, from work by Braun and Oréfice-Okamoto.
- My recollection is that this was extended to degree 5 and that a counterexample with deg p = 6 exists. I am less sure of the exact attribution and wording of that step. The proposed solution's citation for the degree 5 case may be imprecise.

The threshold of 5 is consistent with all of this.

VERDICT: ACCEPT
